title: Regenerate and verify the en.json message catalog with yarn i18n and yarn i18n:check
answers: how do I update en.json after changing UI strings
yarn i18n:check fails what do I run
how to regenerate the default message catalog in mlflow frontend
localized strings catalog out of date
body:
After changing any FormattedMessage defaultMessage/description or intl.formatMessage call in the web-shared trace explorer, run `yarn i18n` from mlflow/server/js to regenerate mlflow/server/js/src/lang/default/en.json.
Run `yarn i18n:check` to confirm the catalog is up to date; CI-style lint checks rely on it.
The regenerated file adds new hashed keys (e.g. for 'Jump to linked span', 'See more') and drops old ones; commit that output with the component change rather than editing keys by hand.
Run `yarn lint`, `yarn prettier:check`, and `yarn type-check` alongside it, as the PR did.
applies: Frontend changes under mlflow/server/js that touch user-visible strings; not needed for non-visible code changes.
says: Frontend continuous integration checks fail because localized user interface strings are out of date.
Update the default translation catalog after modifying visible button labels in trace explorer.
New text labels like jump to linked span are missing from translations.
Automatically verify that all user facing strings match the generated localization messages.
Include updated interface message files whenever changing display text in the trace viewer.

Run yarn i18n:check to verify the catalog is current for CI lint checks, and run yarn lint, yarn prettier:check, and yarn type-check alongside it. Commit the regenerated file rather than editing hashed keys manually; this applies only to changes touching user-visible strings like in the web-shared trace explorer, not to non-visible code changes.
